snippet.description:
In September 2026, the New York Times reports that one AI company is on pace to bring in more than $100 billion a year. The same month, a US appeals court sides against it, with the Pentagon. The company is Anthropic, the maker of Claude. It was started by seven people who walked out of OpenAI together, because they weren't sure powerful AI would go well. So how did the careful ones end up here?

This is the story of Anthropic and Claude, explained simply.

It starts with a boy in San Francisco who didn't care about the internet. Dario Amodei liked maths and studied physics. After his father died of an illness that was cured a few years later, he moved to biology, and then to AI. He joined OpenAI in 2016, and his team built GPT-2 and GPT-3. At the end of 2020, Dario, his sister Daniela and five colleagues left. Anthropic began in 2021, with its first staff eating lunch in a San Francisco park in the middle of a pandemic. In 2022 it held its chatbot, Claude, back; about three months later, OpenAI released ChatGPT. Then came Claude's "constitution", a promise to pause, billions of dollars from Amazon and Google, Claude Code, and a fight with the Pentagon over two exceptions: no mass surveillance of Americans, and no weapons that pick targets and fire on their own.

Then the video follows the money: what Claude is, where Anthropic's money comes from (a draft of its stock-market filing, seen by Reuters, says $4.6 billion in 2025), what it spends on computers, the $518 billion of future computer bills Reuters reports, the authors' lawsuit, what Anthropic says, what happened, and what could happen next. Complex ideas, explained in simple language.
